rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far reads أشهدناهم with the majestic plural; he reads كنت with a fatḥa, addressing the Prophet in wording that functions as a prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ما أشهدناهم } بنون العظمة ، وقرأ { وما كنت } بفتح التاء على الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The misleaders are Satanic beings who instill thoughts of error and corruption, as also described in 6:121.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { المضلين } الشياطين ، لأنهم أضلوا الناس بإلقاء خواطر الضلالة والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause summarizes the denial of witnessing creation; naming the misleaders instead of using a pronoun conveys blame and gives the conclusion independence.
rows.anchor: والعدول عن الإضمار بأن يقال : وما كنت متخذهم إلى { المضلين } لإفادة الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عضد is most eloquently vocalized with fatḥa on ʿayn and ḍamma on ḍād; Banū Tamīm also use two fatḥas, with other weaker variants.
rows.anchor: والعضد بفتح العين وضم الضاد المعجمة في الأفصح ، و بالفتح وسكون الضاد في لغة تميم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributes a two-ḍamma reading of عضد to Abū ʿAmr, transmitted by Hārūn, but says it is not well known.
rows.anchor: ونسب ابن عطية أن أبا عمرو قرأه بضم العين وضم الضاد على أنها لغة في عضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عضد literally names the bone between elbow and shoulder and figuratively means an assistant, as in calling someone one's support.
rows.anchor: وهو : العظم الذي بين المرفق والكتف ، وهو يطلق مجازا على المعين على العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine perfection excludes taking misleaders as helpers in creation: God grants guidance and understanding, so helpers would be expected to resemble the work they assist.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : لا يليق بالكمال الإلهي أن أتخذ أهل الإضلال أعوانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may be linked to the command to prostrate in 18:50, with remember understood, or to 18:51, implying that neither partners were shown creation nor will they help on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم ( الكهف : 50 ) فيقدر : واذكر يوم يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from denying the divinity of Satan and jinn to all idols worshipped by common polytheists, depicting their frustration and despair.
rows.anchor: فهو انتقال من إبطال معبودية الشيطان والجن إلى إبطال إلهية جميع الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument denies divinity by denying a necessary consequence: partners that cannot benefit their worshippers cannot be gods, leaving worshippers in failure and despair.
rows.anchor: الاستدلال على انتفاء الماهية بانتفاء لوازمها ، فإنه إذا انتفى نفعها للذين يعبدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use يقول in the third person, whose subject is God by context; Ḥamza reads نقول with the majestic plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأة الجمهور يقول } بياء الغيبة وضمير الغائب عائد إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene is the Gathering, and the command is directed to polytheists, as الذين زعمتم indicates.
rows.anchor: واليوم الذي يقع فيه هذا القول هو يوم الحشر . والمعنى : يقول للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the idols partners before saying the people alleged this mocks and rebukes them; زعم then marks their claim as false.
rows.anchor: وقدم وصفهم بوصف الشركاء قبل فعل الزعم تهكما بالمخاطبين وتوبيخا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling asks the idols to come for aid or intercession; responding means acknowledging the call and approaching, for example by saying لبّيكم.
rows.anchor: والنداء : طلب الإقبال للنصرة والشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to call the idols is literal but also exposes their falsehood; they call out in hope, and the immediate past-tense narration makes their failure seem instantaneous.
rows.anchor: وأمره إياهم بمناداة شركائهم مستعمل في معناه مع إرادة لازمه وهو إظهار باطلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موبق means a place of destruction; here it is Hell, whose chasms God puts between worshippers and idols, or it is a circumstantial clause preparing for the sight of the Fire in 18:53.
rows.anchor: والموبق هنا أريد به جهنم ، أي حين دعوا أصنامهم بأسمائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause follows the placing of the barrier: criminals are named explicitly to show their deserved punishment, and النار clarifies that the mawbiq is the Fire, almost as apposition.
rows.anchor: فذكر المجرمين إظهار في مقام الإضمار للدلالة على ما يفيده المجرمون من تلبسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ظن here means certainty; its choice may taunt them as merely supposing the Fire was prepared for them when they are in fact certain.
rows.anchor: والظن مستعمل هنا في معنى التحقق وهو من استعمالاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مواقعة is a reciprocal form of وقوع, intensifying the image of their falling into a place that seems to draw them in.
rows.anchor: والمواقعة : مفاعلة من الوقوع ، وهو الحصول لقصد المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مصرف is a place of turning away, meaning escape; the concise wording implies that they try to retreat but find no escape from the Fire.
rows.anchor: والمصرف : مكان الصرف ، أي التخلص والمجاوزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The examples continue earlier parables in 18:32 and 18:45; after showing their persuasive force, the passage praises Quranic guidance, recalling 18:27 and 18:29.
rows.anchor: عطف على الجمل السابقة التي ضربت فيها أمثال من قوله : { واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين ( الكهف : 32 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting في هذا القرآن before للناس, unlike 17:89, foregrounds the Quran because the passage commends its truth rather than human desires.
rows.anchor: إذ قدم هنا قوله : في هذا القرآن } على قوله : { للناس } عكس آية سورة الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الناس generally includes everyone who receives the Quran in future ages, while the immediate target is the polytheists; this is general wording shaped by a particular context.
rows.anchor: والناس : اسم عام لكل من يبلغه القرآن في سائر العصور المستقبلة ، والمقصود على الخصوص المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement about human argumentation implies that the audience disputed the Quran; الإنسان names the human species and is broader than الناس.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : فجادلوا فيه وكان الإنسان أكثر جدلا ، فإن الإنسان اسم لنوع بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human argument can be blameworthy, which Islamic discipline restrains, or praiseworthy: Abraham's debate about Lot's people is praised in 11:74–75.
rows.anchor: ومنه محمود كما في قوله تعالى : { فلما ذهب عن إبراهيم الروع وجاءته البشرى يجادلنا في قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not mean only unbelievers, as in 19:66, or define all argument as false argument, which is specified in 18:56; it prepares for that later charge.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد بالإنسان الإنسان الكافر كما في قوله تعالى : يقول الإنسان أإذا ما مت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شيء is an indefinite, comprehensive singular, making the superlative construction grammatically sound; here the superlative intensifies rather than compares.
rows.anchor: و ( شيء ) اسم مفرد متوغل في العموم . ولذلك صحت إضافة اسم التفضيل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are intensely argumentative even where silence would be better; nonhuman earthly kinds cannot debate, and the wording does not intend comparison with devils or jinn.
rows.anchor: لقصد المبالغة في شدة جدل الإنسان وجنوحه إلى المماراة والنزاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels' debate can be praiseworthy, as in their question and declaration in 2:30; the author rejects taking the superlative as a literal comparison with jinn or devils.
rows.anchor: أما الملائكة فجدلهم محمود مثل قولهم : أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها إلى قوله : ونقدس لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جدلا is an accusative specification of the relation: humans are numerous in argument, meaning that their arguing is abundant.
rows.anchor: وجدلا } تمييز لنسبة الأكثرية إلى الإنسان . والمعنى : وكان الإنسان كثيرا من جهة الجدل

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A sound report says the Prophet woke ʿAlī and Fāṭima at night to pray; ʿAlī answered that God controls their souls and would wake them if He willed.
rows.anchor: ما ثبت في ( الصحيح ) عن علي : ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طرقه وفاطمة ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet left without replying, then struck his thigh and recited the verse; Ibn ʿĀshūr says ʿAlī should have welcomed the wake-up and its reproach rather than use it to defend sleeping.
rows.anchor: ثم سمعته يضرب فخذه ويقول : { وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects a literal ranking of humans above jinn and devils in debate, since that is not intended here and their capacity to debate is unestablished.
rows.anchor: ولا يحسن أن يحمل التفضيل في الآية على بابه بأن يرد أن الإنسان أكثر جدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though this follows naturally from 18:54, it is independently coordinated to give its proposition weight; explicit الناس and الهدى make the statement self-contained.
rows.anchor: ولهذه الخصوصية فيما أرى عدل في هذه الجملة عن الإضمار إلى الإظهار بقوله : وما منع الناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الناس here is broader than in 18:54, including all who refuse belief; guidance includes the Quran, earlier revealed books, and all prophetic teaching.
rows.anchor: وكذلك عموم لفظ الهدى } يشمل هدى القرآن وما قبله من الكتب الإلهية وأقوال الأنبياء كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse draws a historical analogy: these polytheists resemble earlier peoples who received guidance in books, signs, and exhortations but persisted in refusal.
rows.anchor: فكانت هذه الجملة قياسا تمثيليا بشواهد التاريخ وأحوال تلقي الأمم دعوات رسلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the first peoples as earlier deviant, stubborn communities, or as ancestors whose inherited way each later community follows.
rows.anchor: والمرد ب { الأولين } السابقون من الأمم في الضلال والعناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On his reading, nothing distinct prevents these people from belief; they repeat earlier communities' obstinacy, tyranny, rejection of messengers, and contempt for them.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : ما منع هؤلاء المشركين من الإيمان بالقرآن شيء يمنع مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن تأتيهم is a free exception functioning as the subject of منع; ولن يؤمنوا is construed with an omitted preposition, from believing.
rows.anchor: و { أن تأتيهم } استثناء مفرغ هو فاعل { وما منع }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سنة الأولين means their way of unbelief; its genitive is like an agent construction, and attributing the prevention to its arrival is metaphorical imitation of their predecessors.
rows.anchor: وسنة الأولين : طريقتهم في الكفر . وإضافة ( سنة ) إليهم تشبه إضافة المصدر إلى فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أو means until here, with an implied أن before يأتيهم; following the former pattern keeps them from belief until punishment arrives as it did for earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: و ( أو ) هي التي بمعنى ( إلى ) ، وانتصاب فعل يأتيهم العذاب } ( بأن ) مضمرة بعد ( أو )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing prevented them except the same obstinacy, tyranny, and way of denying and slighting messengers that characterized earlier deviants.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : ما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إلا الذي منع الأولين قبلهم من عادة العناد والطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning repentance after belief prompts them to abandon unbelief and repent from rejecting and defying the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وذكر الاستغفار هنا بعد ذكر الإيمان تلقين إياهم بأن يبادروا بالإقلاع عن الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says this interpretation best suits the verse's placement after the preceding discussion.
rows.anchor: هذا ما بدا لي في تفسير هذه الآية وأراه أليق بموقع هاته الآية من التي قبلها

rows.speaker: جميع المفسرين
rows.claim: Other commentators identify these people with the polytheists of 18:54 and guidance with the Quran; they take the phrase as God's established treatment of earlier deniers, namely annihilating punishment.
rows.anchor: فأما جميع المفسرين فقد تأولوا الآية على خلاف هذا على كلمة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That alternative treats the people as waiting for annihilation like earlier nations and reads the verse as a taunting threat that they will believe only when punishment arrives, as in 10:102.
rows.anchor: أي لا يؤمنون إلا عند نزول عذاب الاستيصال

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: In the commentators' alternative reading, قبلا means facing them; al-Kalbī identifies the punishment as the sword at Badr, a face-to-face fighting punishment.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي : وهو عذاب السيف يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading some polytheists suffered the sword in Muslim campaigns while others died to see the afterlife; the verse loses its universal concluding force and becomes only a threat.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا التفسير الذي سلكوه ينسلخ من الآية معنى التذييل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إتيان is metaphorical for future occurrence because أن makes the verb prospective; the future is relative, each community facing the fate of its predecessor.
rows.anchor: والإتيان : مجاز في الحصول في المستقبل ، لوجود ( أن ) المصدرية التي تخلص المضارع للاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سنة is a customary, familiar pattern; attributing prevention to its arrival is a figurative causal attribution, with arrogance, disputation, and attachment to error as the real cause.
rows.anchor: والسنة : العادة المألوفة في حال من الأحوال . وإسناد منعهم الإيمان إلى إتيان سنة الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implication is that they have no valid excuse and will not believe until one of two punishments comes; the warning urges repentance and echoes 10:96–97.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الكناية تهديد وإنذار وتحذير وحث على المبادرة بالاستغفار من الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce قبلا with kasra and fatḥa, meaning face-to-face or plainly; Ḥamza, ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī, Abū Jaʿfar, and Khalaf read it with two ḍammas, a plural meaning kinds.
rows.anchor: وهو بكسر القاف وفتح الباء في قراءة الجمهور بمعنى المقابل الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After noting argumentative resistance in 18:54 and the lack of any obstacle to belief, the passage says messengers convey good news and warning, not debate aimed at guidance.
rows.anchor: أعقب ذلك بأن وظيفة الرسل التبليغ بالبشارة والنذارة لا التصدي للجادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception omits the general circumstances: messengers are sent only while giving glad tidings and warnings, and means all messengers.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء من أحوال عامة محذوفة ، أي ما نرسل المرسلين في حال إلا في حال كونهم مبشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses develop the preceding discussion: messengers offer sufficient guidance, but disbelievers repeatedly argue falsely to erase truth; the imperfect either signals recurrence or makes the scene vivid.
rows.anchor: ولكن الذين كفروا جادلوه بالباطل لإزالة الحق لا لقصد آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جادلنا in 11:74 is a related use of debate; إدحاض means slipping and figuratively means removing, as in 37:141.
rows.anchor: والإدحاض : الإزلاق ، يقال : دحضت القدم ، إذا زلت ، وهو مجاز في الإزالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They debate to defeat truth rather than seek guidance, then mock all signs, especially warnings and reports of resurrection and punishment.
rows.anchor: فإنهم ما قصدوا من المجادلة الاهتداء ، ولكن أرادوا إدحاض الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هزو is a verbal noun meaning that they treated the signs as objects of mockery; they mocked them when hearing resurrection reports and warnings of punishment.
rows.anchor: والهزو : مصدر هزا ، أي اتخذوا ذلك مستهزأ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning what they were warned against after the general word signs is a specific after a general, underscoring the depth of their unbelief and folly.
rows.anchor: وعطف { وما أنذروا } على ( الآيات ) عطف خاص على عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما أنذروا is a masdariyya construction, naming their warning as a verbal noun for emphasis.
rows.anchor: { وما أنذروا } مصدرية ، أي وإنذارهم والإخبار بالمصدر للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce هزءا with ḍamma on zāy; Ḥamza reads its zāy with sukūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { هزءا } بضم الزاي . وقرأه حمزة { هزءا } بسكون الزاي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their bad-faith debate and mockery make them exceptionally unjust to themselves: a rational person would reflect and prepare after warnings of a bad end.
rows.anchor: ذلك لأنه ظلم المرء نفسه وهو أعجب الظلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet asked Quraysh whether they would believe him if he said an enemy would attack the next morning; they admitted his truthfulness, so he warned them of severe punishment.
rows.anchor: إذا أخبرتكم أن العدو مصبحكم غدا أكنتم مصدقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun من is general rather than a named individual, but the context identifies the intended group as Arabian polytheists who rejected the Quran.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها المشركون من العرب الذين ذكروا بالقرآن فأعرضوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ after their being reminded shows that they rushed to turn away without allowing themselves time to consider.
rows.anchor: وعطف إعراضهم عن الذكر على التذكير بفاء التعقيب إشارة إلى أنهم سارعوا بالإعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting past deeds means failing to examine whether they are good or evil and to anticipate their consequences, especially after the Messenger's reminder.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نسيان ما قدمت يداه أنه لم يعرض حاله وأعماله على النظر والفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من is an interrogative used for denial: no one is more unjust than those in view; نسيان here means disregarding, as discussed at 2:106.
rows.anchor: ف ( من ) استفهام مستعمل في الإنكار ، أي لا أحد أظلم من هؤلاء المتحدث عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما قدمت يداه means earlier deeds; the Quran often uses this idiom for evil actions, as in 22:10 and 42:30.
rows.anchor: وأكثر ما يستعمل مثل هذا التركيب في القرآن في العمل السيء ، فصار جاريا مجرى المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though phrased generally, the verse initially targets the Meccan polytheists.
rows.anchor: والآية مصوغة بصيغة العموم ، والمقصود الأول : منها مشركو أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about coverings begins a new explanatory sentence prompted by their forgetting; it explains the outcome rather than functioning grammatically as a reason clause.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إنا جعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة } مستأنفة بيانية نشأت على جملة { ونسي ما قدمت يداه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearts mean faculties of understanding; أكنة is plural of كنان, a covering that conceals; the phrase about understanding has an omitted من because أكنة implies a barrier.
rows.anchor: والقلوب مراد بها : مدارك العلم . والأكنة : جمع كنان ، وهو الغطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقر means heaviness of hearing that prevents sound reaching the ear's inner passage; the pronoun in يفقهوه refers contextually to the Quran, also called the signs.
rows.anchor: والوقر : ثقل السمع المانع من وصول الصوت إلى الصماخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitation to guidance is coordinated with the covering statement and develops from it, but is not introduced with fa because it is presented as an independent report.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وإن تدعهم إلى الهدى } عطف على جملة { إنا جعلنا على قلوبهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their never being guided is emphatically denied by لن, أبدا, and a conditional-result construction; the result follows from hearts formed not to accept truth.
rows.anchor: وأكد نفي اهتدائهم بحرف توكيد النفي وهو ( لن ) ، وبلفظ ( أبدا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After threats, the Quran recalls forgiveness and mercy to invite reflection, gratitude, and return: God delays punishment to a fixed term; the address to the Prophet honors him through the Lord's care, as in 8:33.
rows.anchor: فلما رماهم بقوارع التهديد والوعيد عطف على ذلك التعريض بالتذكير بالمغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He construes الغفور as an adjective of the subject and ذو الرحمة as predicate, fitting the context and next conditional; الغفور also indirectly urges repentance.
rows.anchor: والوجه في نظم الآية أن يكون الغفور } نعتا للمبتدأ ويكون { ذو الرحمة } هو الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الغفور intensifies God's vast forgiveness of countless repentant servants and sins; delaying punishment is itself a temporary form of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: والغفور : اسم يتضمن مبالغة الغفران لأنه تعالى واسع المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذو الرحمة prepares for the conditional: although their shirk and defiance merit immediate punishment, delay grants time for reconsideration and is mercy to people.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم فيما كسبوه من الشرك والعناد أحرياء بتعجيل العقوبة لكن الله يمهلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذو expresses a firmly rooted relation; using ذو الرحمة instead of الرحيم marks it as predicate, since the latter's intensive-adjective form seems almost like a fixed attribute.
rows.anchor: وإنما عدل عن وصف ( الرحيم ) إلى { ذو الرحمة } للتنبيه على أنه خبر لا نعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل cancels the conditional consequence: punishment was not hastened because its appointment is delayed, a threat realized at Badr.
rows.anchor: و ( بل ) للإضراب الإبطالي عن مضمون جواب ( لو ) ، أي لم يعجل لهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موئل derives from وأل, to seek refuge, and means a place of refuge.
rows.anchor: والموئل : مفعل من وأل بمعنى لجأ ، فهو اسم مكان بمعنى الملجأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لن emphatically answers their assumption that a long delay means escape: no refuge from the punishment outside its appointed time or place, an assertion reinforced by apparent contradiction.
rows.anchor: وأكد النفي ب ( لن ) ردا على إنكارهم ، إذ هم يحسبون أنهم مفلتون من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fate of earlier towns illustrates that delay, explained as mercy in 18:58, does not save them; their destruction followed their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ضرب لهم المثل في ذلك بحال أهل القرى السالفين الذين أخر عنهم العذاب مدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those cities are mentally present: Arabs knew the homes of ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Midian and heard of Lot's and Pharaoh's peoples; the demonstrative's kāf is not an actual addressee.
rows.anchor: والعرب يعرفون ديار عاد وثمود ومدين ويسمعون بقوم لوط وقوم فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wrongdoing means associating partners with God and denying the messengers.
rows.anchor: والظلم : الشرك وتكذيب الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers take مَهْلِك as a verbal noun of أهلك, the appointed time in God's knowledge; Ḥafṣ reads مَهْلِك as a time noun, while Abū Bakr reads مَهْلَك as a verbal noun of هلك.
rows.anchor: هذه قراءة الجمهور . وقرأه حفص عن عاصم بفتح الميم وكسر اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Adam and Iblis depicts pride, contempt for virtue, and envy; Moses' story contrasts it with seeking greater knowledge and recognizing another's excellence, teaching believers and refuting unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أعقب تلك القصة بقصة هي مثل في ضدها لأن تطلب ذي الفضل والكمال للازدياد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the sura answered questions about the Cave and Dhū al-Qarnayn, it now turns to its second account; Moses' learning journey parallels travel for benefit and hints that People of the Book should share prophetic wisdom, not tales of empire.
rows.anchor: وقد تقضى الجواب عن القصة الأولى وما ذيلت به ، وآن أن ينتقل إلى الجواب عن القصة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ قال موسى coordinates this story with the angels' prostration story in 18:50; understand remember, with إذ as its object, since both stories teach and admonish.
rows.anchor: فجملة { وإذ قال موسى } معطوفة على جملة { وإذ قلنا للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتى means a young male and figuratively a companion, attendant, or servant; compare its use in 12:30.
rows.anchor: والفتى : الذكر الشاب ، والأنثى فتاة ، وهو مستعمل مجازا في التابع والخادم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr could not be an Israelite governed by Moses' law, since Moses could not approve his unlawful acts; he must have been a prophet given distinct revelation and belonging to another community.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون الخضر من بني إسرائيل إذ لا يجوز أن يكون مكلفا بشريعة موسى

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: In the report from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, God tells Moses that His servant Khidr knows what Moses does not; this revealed that Khidr had a separate law.
rows.anchor: كما في حديث أبي بن كعب ، لم يصرفه عنه ما رأى من أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's presence in Israelite territory was either devotional travel or God's arrangement for the meeting place, as a kindness to Moses.
rows.anchor: وأما وجوده في أرض بني إسرائيل فهو من السياحة في العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمضي means to go or travel; حقب is an indefinitely long period, plural أحقاب.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أو أمضي } أو أسير . والمضي : الذهاب والسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction makes reaching the confluence or continuing for a long time alternative endpoints; Moses was certain by revelation that he would arrive, so it intensifies resolve, discourages return, or steels his attendant.
rows.anchor: فصار المعطوف إحدى غايتين للإقلاع عن السير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa is both consequential and explanatory, unpacking an omitted statement that they travelled until they reached the confluence; بينهما refers to the place joining the two seas.
rows.anchor: الفاء للتفريع والفصيحة لأنها تفصح عن كلام مقدر ، أي فسارا حتى بلغا مجمع البحرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding مجمع to بين is an extended construction: بين normally acts as an adverb but can be governed as a noun, as in 5:106, or used without annexation in one reading of 6:94.
rows.anchor: وشأنه في اللغة أن يكون ظرفا للفعل ، ولكنه قد يستعمل لمجرد مكان متوسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had instructed Moses to carry the fish as a sign marking where to find Khidr, as related in the preceding hadith.
rows.anchor: والحوت هو الذي أمر الله موسى باستصحابه معه ليكون له علامة على المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both forgot to watch whether the fish was still in its basket, so they missed the sign; although Yusha was assigned to guard it, Moses too had to supervise the task he needed.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نسيانهما أنهما نسيا أن يراقبا حاله أباقق هو في مكتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses slept while his attendant stayed awake; the fish stirred and made a path through the sea.
rows.anchor: ثم إن موسى عليه السلام نام وبقي فتاه يقظان فاضطرب الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سرب is a tunnel and اتخذ means make; سربا is a circumstantial simile, illustrated by Imruʾ al-Qays's line whose phrase بريا القرنفل evokes carnation fragrance.
rows.anchor: والسرب : النفق . والاتخاذ : الجعل . وقد انتصب سربا } على الحال من { سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object after جاوزا is the confluence of the seas.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول { جاوزا } للعلم ، أي جاوزا مجمع البحرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غداء is the daytime meal, named from the early day; its opposite is supper, and نصب means fatigue.
rows.anchor: والغداء : طعام النهار مشتق من كلمة الغدوة لأنه يؤكل في وقت الغدوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rock was the familiar resting place at the confluence; an anonymous report locates it below a river called the Oil River for its many olive trees.
rows.anchor: والصخرة : صخرة معهودة لهما ، إذ كانا قد أويا إليها في سيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting the fish means forgetting to guard and check on it, allowing it to escape.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { نسيت الحوت } أي نسيت حفظه وافتقاده ، أي فانفلت في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second forgetting is distinct: Yusha forgot to tell Moses about the incident, rather than forgetting the fish again.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره } . هذا نسيان آخر غير النسيان الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads أنسانيه with a ḍamma on the pronoun hāʾ; kasra is more common because it is lighter after yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم { وما أنسانيه } بضم هاء الضمير على أصل الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن أذكره is an explanatory apposition to the pronoun in أنسانيه, not to the fish; remembering here means verbal mention to Moses.
rows.anchor: و { أن أذكره } بدل اشتمال من ضمير { أنسانيه } لا من الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the event was recent, extraordinary, and important, Yusha's failure to report it must be Satanic distraction; he knew Satan opposed the beneficial meeting and learning it would enable.
rows.anchor: يتعين أن الشيطان ألهاه بأشياء عن أن يتذكر ذلك الحادث العجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: And it took its way in the sea continues Yusha's speech: the fish swam after having long been dead.
rows.anchor: وجملة { واتخذ سبيله في البحر } عطف على جملة { فإني نسيت الحوت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's earlier hadith explains how the fish made a tunnel through the water.
rows.anchor: وقد مر تفسير كيف اتخذ البحر سربا في الحديث السابق عن أبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من marks source: mercy and knowledge come from the honored nearness of God; Khidr's authority or prophethood and rare knowledge are gifts reserved for the chosen.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) ابتدائية ، أي آتيناه رحمة صدرت من مكان القرب ، أي الشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing من عندنا to من لدنا is stylistic variation that avoids repeating the same expression.
rows.anchor: والمخالفة بين من عندنا } وبين { من لدنا } للتفنن تفاديا من إعادة الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' words begin a fresh dialogue, hence an initial independent sentence rather than a connective قال.
rows.anchor: وجملة { قال له موسى } ابتداء محاورة ، فهو استئناف ابتدائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هل أتبعك is an offer or request, since Moses asks about his own action; following metaphorically means companionship, as in 53:28.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام في قوله : { هل أتبعك } مستعمل في العرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على signals a condition or commitment: following is framed as undertaken in return for teaching, in a formula resembling a contract.
rows.anchor: و ( على ) مستعملة في معنى الاشتراط لأنه استعلاء مجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports contracts to teach Quran and knowledge; a hadith describes the Prophet marrying a woman to a man in exchange for teaching her the Quran.
rows.anchor: ويؤخذ من الآية جواز التعاقد على تعليم القرآن والعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such commitments must be honored; teaching custom can function as an implied term, requiring teachers to follow local norms.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه التزام يجب الوفاء به . وقد تفرع عن حكم لزوم الالتزام أن العرف فيه يقوم مقام الاشتراط

rows.speaker: عياض
rows.claim: In al-Madārik, ʿIyāḍ recounts a Khurasani who travelled to hear Mālik; when local custom conflicted over reading aloud, the judge ruled that Mālik should read to him, and Mālik agreed the ruling was right.
rows.anchor: وذكر عياض في باب صفة مجلس مالك للعلم من كتاب المدارك : أن رجلا خراسانيا جاء من خراسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also implies that the learner should follow and emulate the teacher.
rows.anchor: وفيه أيضا إشارة إلى أن حق المعلم على المتعلم اتباعه والاقتداء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رشدا is the direct object of teach: what brings right guidance, namely good.
rows.anchor: وانتصب رشدا } على المفعولية ل { تعلمن } أي ما به الرشد ، أي الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seeks useful knowledge outside Israelite legislation, which he receives directly by revelation; prophecy does not require every kind of worldly knowledge, as the date-pollination report and Badr site consultation illustrate.
rows.anchor: وهذا العلم الذي سأل موسى تعلمه هو من العلم النافع الذي لا يتعلق بالتشريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seeks Khidr's special useful knowledge in keeping with 20:114; it is particularized policy for helping or protecting specific people, unlike general public law.
rows.anchor: وإنما رام موسى أن يعلم شيئا من العلم الذي خص الله به الخضر لأن الازدياد من العلوم النافعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction resembles prophetic knowledge of some unbelievers' or hypocrites' inward states while continuing to call them to faith or treating them as believers; the Prophet disclosed hypocrite identities to Ḥudhayfa.
rows.anchor: ونظيره معرفة النبي أحوال بعض المشركين والمنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers say رُشدا with ḍamma and sukūn; Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb use fatḥa on both, two lexical variants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور رشدا } بضم الراء وسكون الشين . وقرأه أبو عمرو ، ويعقوب بفتح الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إِنَّكَ لَن emphasizes Khidr's warning because he expects Moses to struggle with acts whose outward appearance is wrong though their hidden purpose is right; Moses enforces revealed law by appearances.
rows.anchor: وأكد جملة { إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا } بحرف ( إن ) وبحرف ( لن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's words are a caution that lets Moses choose knowingly, not merely a prediction; the emphasis underscores how strange and difficult the coming acts will appear.
rows.anchor: وهذا تحذير منه لموسى وتنبيه على ما يستقبله منه حتى يقدم على متابعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching should include warning learners about difficulties in their subject, especially when studying it will be hard.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا أصل من أصول التعليم أن ينبه المعلم المتعلم بعوارض موضوعات العلوم الملقنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative patience is intensified by indefinite ṣabr under negation, لن, إن, and inability itself: even trying to endure would fail; معي narrows the difficulty to Moses' company with Khidr.
rows.anchor: وزادها تأكيدا عموم الصبر المنفي لوقوعه نكرة في سياق النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: How can you endure is circumstantial yet functions as the inseparable cause of the preceding claim; it is an interrogative denial meaning you cannot endure.
rows.anchor: فالواو واو الحال وليست واو العطف لأن شأن هذه الجملة أن لا تعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خبر means knowledge; it specifies the scope of إحاطة, while إحاطة metaphorically describes complete mastery as if physically enclosing something.
rows.anchor: والخبر بضم الخاء وسكون الباء : العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You will find me patient promises observable endurance more strongly than I will be patient; this includes travel fatigue, strange actions, and waiting to understand their reasons.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا } أبلغ في ثبوت الصبر من نحو : سأصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding that he will not disobey any command makes obedience part of ideal student conduct; patience and obedience are the learner's key qualities.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن أهم ما يتسم به طالب العلم هو الصبر والطاعة للمعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking God's will seeks help and shows courtesy: learned students may object more readily when a teacher's unfamiliar material conflicts with existing knowledge, risking discord.
rows.anchor: وفي تأكيده ذلك بالتعليق على مشيئة الله استعانة به وحرصا على تقدم التيسير تأدبا مع الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' promise rests on trusting Khidr's protection, since God had told him Khidr possessed knowledge.
rows.anchor: والتزام موسى ذلك مبني على ثقته بعصمة متبوعه لأن الله أخبره بأنه آتاه علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition follows Moses' promise: Khidr tells him not to ask about anything he sees until Khidr himself explains it.
rows.anchor: ففرع على ذلك نهيه عن السؤال عن شيء مما يشاهده من تصرفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic prohibition protects the teacher's timing; questions might interrupt work and provoke rushed, anxious, incomplete answers, whereas a chosen moment allows clearer explanation and rapport.
rows.anchor: لأن السؤال قد يصادف وقت اشتغال المسؤول بإكمال عمله فتضيق له نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذكر means spoken explanation of causes and clarification of mysteries, as at 2:40; إحداث الذكر means bringing that explanation into existence.
rows.anchor: والذكر ، هنا : ذكر اللسان . وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line by Dhū al-Rumma illustrates إحداث as creating or producing something.
rows.anchor: وإحداث الذكر : إنشاؤه وإبرازه ، كقول ذي الرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads فلا تسألني with hamza, fatḥa on lām, doubled nūn of emphasis, and the first-person yāʾ; Ibn ʿĀmir matches but omits the yāʾ, while the rest keep hamza, sukūn lām, single nūn, and yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع فلا تسألني } بالهمز وبفتح اللام وتشديد النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their departure follows the dialogue; انطلاق means going or walking and derives from release, since an untethered animal moves.
rows.anchor: والانطلاق : الذهاب والمشي ، مشتق من الإطلاق وهو ضد التقييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى marks the endpoint of their setting out, while it also begins a new sentence; omitted wording says they hired and boarded a ship before Khidr punctured it.
rows.anchor: و ( حتى ) ابتدائية ، وفي الكلام إيجاز دل عليه قوله : { إذا ركبا في السفينة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: السفينة is definite through mental familiarity, like الذئب in 12:13.
rows.anchor: وتعريف { السفينة } تعريف العهد الذهني ، مثل التعريف في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذا locates past time rather than a condition; puncturing at the instant of boarding suggests the act was planned beforehand, with the fronted timing emphasized.
rows.anchor: وإذا } ظرف للزمان الماضي هنا ، وليست متضمنة معنى الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ركبا في means entering the ship, a figurative boarding construction also seen in 11:41, unlike ordinary riding wording such as 16:8.
rows.anchor: وضمن الركوب معنى الدخول لأنه ركوب مجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خرق is to pierce or split, the opposite of joining; Moses' interrogative objects to the apparent aim of drowning the passengers, and إمرا denotes a grave, alarming wrong.
rows.anchor: والخرق : الثقب والشق ، وهو ضد الالتئام . والاستفهام في أخرقتها } للإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets confront wrongdoing forcefully; Moses calls it إمرا rather than نكرا because the ship has not actually sunk and the act is only a means to harm.
rows.anchor: ولم يجعله نكرا كما في الآية بعدها لأن العلم الذي عمله الخضر ذريعة للغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use the addressed form لتغرق; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read ليغرق and make أهلها the nominative subject, the ship's people drowning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { لتغرق } بمثناة فوقية مضمومة على الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question seeks acknowledgment and gently reproaches Moses for not keeping his commitment: do you admit I said you could not endure with me?
rows.anchor: استفهام تقرير وتعريض باللوم على عدم الوفاء بما التزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معي restricts the denied ability to endure to Khidr's company, where Moses sees marvels he cannot interpret.
rows.anchor: فاستطاعة الصبر المنفية هي التي تكون في صحبته لأنه يرى أمورا عجيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of the saying is omitted, treating the statement as complete in itself: did I not say words warning you of inability?
rows.anchor: وحذف متعلق القول تنزيلا له منزلة اللازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses attributes his lapse to forgetfulness, his promise having slipped from mind under the shock of seeing what he considered wrong.
rows.anchor: اعتذر موسى بالنسيان وكان قد نسي التزامه بما غشي ذهنه من مشاهدة ما ينكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is a tender plea for leniency, not a blunt excuse; Moses asks not to be blamed, apparently accepting that forgetfulness could make him unfit for companionship.
rows.anchor: والنهي مستعمل في التعطف والتماس عدم المؤاخذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مؤاخذة is a reciprocal form used intensively despite the action coming from one side, as in 16:61.
rows.anchor: والمؤاخذة : مفاعلة من الأخذ ، وهي هنا للمبالغة لأنها من جانب واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is masdariyya, meaning my forgetting; إرهاق means overwhelming or covering, metaphorically harsh treatment, and عسر is severity, here lack of leniency.
rows.anchor: و ( ما ) مصدرية ، أي لا تؤاخذني بنسياني . والإرهاق : تعدية رهق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمر means affair; من may mark the source, so forgetfulness leads to harsh treatment, or clarify the affair, meaning Moses' situation with Khidr.
rows.anchor: والأمر : الشأن . و ( من ) يجوز أن تكون ابتدائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition after Moses' apology shows Khidr accepted it and they continued together; the sentence structure follows the ship episode.
rows.anchor: يدل تفريع قوله : { فانطلقا حتى إذا لقيا غلاما } عن اعتذار موسى ، على أن الخضر قبل عذره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted timing shows Khidr killed the boy immediately upon meeting him, even more swiftly than he punctured the ship after boarding.
rows.anchor: فكانت المبادرة بقتل الغلام عند لقائه أسرع من المبادرة بخرق السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses objects in the same pattern but calls this act نكر, an intellectually repugnant actual harm stronger than إمرا, which was only a route to possible harm.
rows.anchor: وصف هذا الفعل بأنه نكر ، وهو بضمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is pure because the boy had not reached puberty and committed no sin; زكاء means increase in goodness.
rows.anchor: ووصف النفس بالزاكية لأنها نفس غلام لم يبلغ الحلم فلم يقترف ذنبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, and Ruways read زاكية with an alif; the rest read زكية, with both forms meaning the same.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، وأبو جعفر ، ورويس عن يعقوب { زاكية } بألف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the nūn of نكرا is the midpoint of the Quran's letters; Ibn ʿĀshūr notes the majority instead place its midpoint at the tāʾ in 18:19.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : النون من قوله : { نكرا } هي نصف القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr repeats his earlier answer but adds لك, explicitly identifying the listener to confirm and strengthen the reproach because Moses had ignored the warning.
rows.anchor: والداعي لذلك أنه أهمل العمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لك is the communicative lām used with a known recipient; naming it increases force, unlike the first answer, which omitted it.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله { لك } لام التبليغ ، وهي التي تدخل على اسم أو ضمير السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses does not repeat the forgetfulness excuse: either he deliberately prioritized stopping the grave murder, or he had forgotten but found repeated excuses unseemly; the Prophet's report allows both readings.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث عن النبي : كانت الأولى من موسى نسيانا ، والثانية شرطا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is fair to Khidr by granting him grounds to end their companionship after another question, avoiding putting him in an awkward position.
rows.anchor: وأنصف موسى إذ جعل لصاحبه العذر في ترك مصاحبته في الثالثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers geminate the nūn in لدني; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this is a reading transmitted specifically from the Prophet, as noted in the commentary's sixth introduction.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { لدني } بتشديد النون قال ابن عطية : وهي قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū Bakr, and Abū Jaʿfar read لدني with a light nūn, dropping the protective nūn for ease because لدن is heavier than عن and من.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وأبو بكر ، وأبو جعفر { من لدني بتخفيف النون على أنه حذف منه نون الوقاية
